newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Japanese seek $50 mln for Ven aluminum veto - paper.
newsitem.headline: Japanese seek $50 mln for Ven aluminum veto - paper.

text.p: Japanese shareholders in Venezuelan smelter Venalum asked for $50 million in return for relinquishing their veto power in the company, Venezuelan Investment Fund (FIV) President Alberto Poletto was quoted as saying Thursday.

Poletto said the Venezuelan government had rejected the offer not because of the sum but because of other demands made by the Japanese consortium which holds 20 percent of Venalum, local daily El Globo reported Thursday.
Poletto said the government was also reluctant to continue a contract to supply 90,000 tonnes per year of aluminum to the Japanese consortium.

The Venezuelans are also unwilling to allow the Japanese to hold a stake in the fused aluminum sector complex when Venalum is fused with smelter Alcasa, carbon anode producer Carbonorca and bauxite producer Bauxilum later this year.
No comment was immediately from Venalum and Poletto's office on the El Globo report.
The Venezuelan government aims to sell-off a controlling stake in the state-owned aluminum sector by the end of the year.
Poletto and other government officials held talks with the Japanese consortium in Tokyo last week and have planned further talks in Caracas for the end of September.
The Japanese consortium includes Showa Denko KK, Kobe Steel Ltd, Sumitomo Chemical Co Ltd, Mitsubishi Materials Corp, Mitsubishi Aluminum Co Ltd and Marubeni Corp.
